title: Variables and Data Types
description: Master the foundation of C# programming: variables, value types, reference types, and type conversion. Build confidence in how C# stores and transforms data.
longDescription: Before you can write meaningful C# programs, you need to understand how the language stores and manages data. This module introduces the core type system that underpins every C# application. You will learn how to declare and initialize variables, when to use the `var` keyword, and why naming conventions matter. You will then explore the two fundamental categories of C# types — value types (stored directly on the stack) and reference types (stored on the heap with pointer indirection) — and see how their different memory behavior affects assignment, method calls, and comparison. Finally, you will learn how to safely convert between types using implicit conversions, explicit casts, `Parse`/`TryParse`, and the `Convert` class, with attention to common pitfalls like truncation and overflow.
whatYouLearn: Declare and initialize variables with explicit types and var
Use const and readonly for immutable values
Distinguish value types from reference types
Understand stack vs heap memory layout
Work with integers, floating-point, char, bool, and structs
Use classes, strings, arrays, and List<T>
Perform implicit and explicit type conversions
Use TryParse for safe string-to-number conversion
Avoid common pitfalls like NullReferenceException and truncation
